title: Dark Venture (Kickstarter Preview) - Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N54m3zy-uzk

Daniel (@dungeondive) went looking for this one himself. Unpaid and unsolicited: he spotted Dark Venture on Kickstarter, decided the art was "pure Dungeon Dive style," and wrote to designer Rob Lemon asking to make a video. Lemon sent a prototype with eight days left on the campaign.

What arrives is an adventure card game for one to four players that hides an enormous amount of game in a very small box. The closest comparison Daniel reaches for is Dungeoneer — players hold a hand of location, character and item cards and build the world themselves, tile by tile, rather than having the game deal it out. Each new location carries a blue paragraph in a pocket-sized location guide and often a green number pointing into a separate actions book, where the game turns briefly into interactive fiction: read the map, destroy the map, get in the boat, untie the boat.

Enemies and NPCs are built exactly like heroes — full stats, equipped gear, lootable corpses — which gives the world weight and slows the game down in equal measure. Twelve rounds run sunrise to sunset while you chase one heroic quest and a rolling three side quests.

The influences are named outright: TSR, Gamma World, and the grotesque line work of City of Chaos. Daniel also confesses he has been slowly building something similar himself for about a year.

----

Player-built maps and player-placed enemies put the whole world in the hands of the people exploring it. Does that make discovery more satisfying for you, or less?
